Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.testing

Class RefreshDatabase

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.testing.RefreshDatabase
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.AfterEachCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.BeforeAllCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.BeforeEachCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.Extension, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ParameterResolver, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.TestInstantiationAwareExtension
public final class RefreshDatabase extends Object implements org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.BeforeAllCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.BeforeEachCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.AfterEachCallback, org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ParameterResolver
A JUnit 5 extension that gives every test an empty database with the migrations applied.

The migrations run once per test run, through Migrator.fresh(), the first time a test class that uses the extension starts. Later classes with the same connection instance and the same migration list reuse that schema. The same connection with a different list in the same run is refused with an IllegalStateException: migrating again would drop the tables of the classes that already ran. The record lives in the root store of the JUnit run, so it is shared by every class of the run. The migration list is compared by migration class and name, so editing the body of a migration within one run is not noticed.

Three modes decide how a test's data is removed:

  • rollback(java.util.function.Supplier<org.aristonis.diwan.database.query.QueryFactory>, java.util.function.Function<org.aristonis.diwan.database.Connection, org.aristonis.diwan.database.schema.Schema>, java.util.List<org.aristonis.diwan.database.migrations.Migration>) opens a transaction before each test and rolls it back after. Calls the test makes through the root connection from its own thread run inside that transaction, even with strict transactions on, and transaction(...) becomes a savepoint. Callbacks of Connection.afterCommit(Runnable) registered inside never run, because nothing commits. Work done on other threads, such as threads or executors the test starts, or a test under @Timeout(threadMode = SEPARATE_THREAD), is not part of the transaction and commits for real. Tests may run in parallel, one transaction per test thread. Sequences are not rolled back, so on PostgreSQL the ids a test gets depend on the tests that ran before it. restartingIdentities() sets them back before each test, to the value after the highest committed id: rows a migration or a seeder committed are kept, so the first new row gets the id after them, and the same ids every time. It needs PostgreSQL 10 or later, does nothing on SQLite, whose rollback already restores its counters, and refuses parallel tests, which share the sequences; Gradle forks that use one database are not detected, so give each fork its own database.
  • truncate(java.util.function.Supplier<org.aristonis.diwan.database.query.QueryFactory>, java.util.function.Function<org.aristonis.diwan.database.Connection, org.aristonis.diwan.database.schema.Schema>, java.util.List<org.aristonis.diwan.database.migrations.Migration>) lets the test commit for real and empties every table except the migrations table after it, in one QueryFactory.truncate(List) call, so identities restart. Slower, but afterCommit callbacks run and other threads see the data. Internal tables, such as PostGIS's spatial_ref_sys, are left alone, and a table counts only when its name starts with the table prefix of the connection. The list of tables is read once per run, after the first test, so a table a test creates later is not emptied. Tests must not run in parallel in this mode: it fails with an IllegalStateException under ExecutionMode.CONCURRENT; use rollback mode, or @Execution(ExecutionMode.SAME_THREAD).
  • template(DataSource, Function, Function, List) gives every test its own database, a copy of a template that holds the migrated schema. The migrations run once per migration list, into a template database that later runs reuse; each test copies it, and the copy is dropped after the test. The test may commit, use other threads and run in parallel, and sequences start over. It needs PostgreSQL, where the role can create databases, or SQLite with directory(Path); an in-memory SQLite database is refused. The extension holds one connection on the root data source for the whole run, so give it a plain driver data source or a pool in session mode. strategy(CopyStrategy), directory(Path) and dropStaleTemplates() tune it. The parameters below come from the test's own database.

Register it in a field of the test class, static or not: 


 @RegisterExtension
 static RefreshDatabase db = RefreshDatabase.rollback(
         () -> SQLiteQuery.of(connection), SQLiteSchema::of, migrations);

 @Test
 void savesAUser(DatabaseAssertions assertions, QueryFactory query) {
     query.table("users").insert(Map.of("name", "ann"));
     assertions.assertCount("users", 1);
 }

Test methods may declare parameters of type DatabaseAssertions, QueryFactory and Connection; the extension resolves them from the supplied query factory.

The supplier must return the same connection instance every time, which identifies the database. Instances are safe to share between tests; the suppliers and the function must be safe to call from the test thread.

Requirements: JUnit 5.10 or later (the extension was not run against 5.x). The eloquent module is needed only by the model assertions. dropAllTables on PostgreSQL drops tables, not types, sequences or functions, so a migration that creates one drops it itself, or the schema of the tests is a dedicated one.

    • template

      public static RefreshDatabase template(DataSource root, Function<String,DatabaseManager> perDatabase, Function<Connection,Schema> schema, List<Migration> migrations)
      Creates an extension that gives every test its own copy of a migrated template database.

      The template is named after the migration list, class, name and checksum of each migration in order, so a run with the same list reuses the template an earlier run built, and a changed list builds a new one; older templates stay unless dropStaleTemplates() is set. Runs that start together, in this or in other JVMs, build it once. Copies and build databases that a run which died left behind are removed at the start of the next run.

      Parameters:
      root - the data source of the server that holds the databases, never null; the extension takes one connection from it and holds it until the run ends
      perDatabase - opens a manager on the database of the given name, never null; the extension closes it after each test and after migrating the template. On SQLite the name is the path of the file to open. It must not keep a session open on the template
      schema - builds the schema builder for a connection, never null
      migrations - the migrations that build the test schema, never null, without null elements; copied
      Returns:
      the extension, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument or an element is null

    • strategy

      public RefreshDatabase strategy(CopyStrategy strategy)
      Returns an extension like this one that sends a copy strategy when it creates each copy.

      Without it, PostgreSQL 15 or later gets FILE_COPY and older servers get none. An explicit strategy on a server older than 15 fails with an UnsupportedOperationException when the first copy is made.

      Parameters:
      strategy - the strategy, never null
      Returns:
      a new extension with the option set; this one is not changed, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if strategy is null
      IllegalStateException - if this extension is not in template mode

    • dropStaleTemplates

      public RefreshDatabase dropStaleTemplates()
      Returns an extension like this one that also drops the templates of other migration lists at the start of a run.

      Without it older templates stay on the server or in the directory. On PostgreSQL a template that another live run is copying from cannot be dropped; the refusal is logged and the run goes on. On SQLite the other templates' files are deleted with their side and lock files, except a template whose build lock another holder has.

      Returns:
      a new extension with the option set; this one is not changed, never null
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if this extension is not in template mode

    • restartingIdentities

      public RefreshDatabase restartingIdentities()
      Returns an extension like this one that also sets the identity and serial counters back before each test, so the test sees the ids it would see on a freshly migrated database.

      Only rollback mode needs it: a rollback leaves the PostgreSQL sequences where the test moved them, while truncate mode restarts them already. Before each test, after the migrations ran and before the test's transaction opens, the counters of the tables the extension owns are set to the value after the highest committed id, or to the start value of an empty table; see QueryFactory.restartIdentities(List). The table list is read once per run, right after the migrations, so a table a test creates later is not restarted. This needs PostgreSQL 10 or later and does nothing on SQLite. Tests must not run in parallel with this option: they share the sequences, and the extension fails with an IllegalStateException under ExecutionMode.CONCURRENT. The check sees one JVM, so Gradle forks that use one database are not caught.

      Returns:
      a new extension with the option on; this one is not changed, never null
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if this extension is in truncate mode, which restarts identities already, or in template mode, where every test starts on a fresh copy
